question: The Work Explorer and the CLI checklist cannot say which step a session is currently on, because no writer ever produces an in-progress step status. Should the missing state be WRITTEN by a new or extended writer, or DERIVED at read time from rows both surfaces already read?
decision: Derive, never write. The active step is computed in the one Python row derivation (build_rows) and its TypeScript mirror as the lowest-numbered seeded plan-step row with nothing logged against it, in a session session-state.json reports as in flight. No writer changes, and nothing is stored on disk to make it true.

options.option: Derive it at read time from the seeded plan rows plus session-state.json (Option 2 in the source-of-record note).
options.consequence: No writer change and no orchestrator convention to remember; it cannot drift out of sync because it is computed from the same rows the tree already reads; and it fixes every historical set retroactively. Costs a second implementation of the predicate (Python and TypeScript), which is why a cross-language parity falsifier is scheduled in Session 2.

options.option: Option 1 from the note: log an in_progress entry on ENTERING each step.
options.consequence: Doubles every log_step call and depends on an orchestrator convention this repo keeps having to replace with a gate; the on-disk evidence (in-progress is ~1.4% of every step status ever written, and appears in no current set) is what that convention already decayed to. Fixes nothing historical, and adds a writer that can drift from reality whenever a session dies mid-step.

options.option: Option 3 from the note: start_session stamps step 1 as in-progress.
options.consequence: Option 1 with extra steps, and wrong from step 2 onward -- it would assert the session is on step 1 for the entire session. Fixes nothing historical and adds a state-file-adjacent writer for a display concern.

rationale: Taken at spec authoring (docs/session-sets/127-the-active-step-shows-in-progress/spec.md, Scope: 'Option 2 from the note -- derive it'), journalled at Session 1 registration with the spec cited as origin. prefer-reversible decides it: a pure read-time derivation can be deleted in one commit and leaves no residue on disk, while a new writer's output becomes historical record the moment it runs and cannot be un-written from sets that already closed. goal-over-letter points the same way -- the goal is that the operator can see where a session is, including in sets that closed months ago, and only the derivation reaches those. The rejected options are recorded here so they are not re-opened mid-set.

question: The derived in-flight step state is a new signal in a workflow full of machine-enforced gates. Should it be allowed to affect anything other than what is shown to the operator -- an exit code, the log_step vocabulary, or a close gate?
decision: Display-only. The derived state changes no exit code, adds nothing to the log_step status vocabulary, and nothing is stored on disk. It is read by the checklist renderer, the projection, and the tree, and by nothing that decides whether a session may close.

options.option: Display-only: the derivation reaches renderers and the projection, and no gate, exit code, or writer.
options.consequence: The blast radius is what an operator sees. A wrong derivation shows a wrong glyph, which is bad but visible and instantly fixable; it cannot refuse a close or corrupt a record. Keeps the change deletable in one commit.

options.option: Let the derived state feed a gate (e.g. refuse to close while a step is derived in flight, or warn on an exit code).
options.consequence: Would make a derived, heuristic signal load-bearing for close-out. A derivation that is wrong on an edge case would then block real work, and callers and CI would adapt to the new exit code, making it expensive to walk back.

options.option: Add in-progress to the log_step status vocabulary so the derivation and the writer share one token.
options.consequence: Re-opens the rejected write-it option through the side door, and re-introduces the convention the derivation exists to remove.

rationale: Taken at spec authoring (docs/session-sets/127-the-active-step-shows-in-progress/spec.md, Session 1 Step 1 and the 'No new writer' non-goal), journalled at Session 1 registration with the spec cited as origin. prefer-reversible decides it: keeping a new signal out of every gate and exit code is what makes the whole set removable, and it bounds the worst case of a mis-derivation to a wrong glyph rather than a refused close. This decision REDUCES nothing about verification -- it withholds a new signal from the gates rather than weakening an existing check -- so it is not a verification-reduction call and remains AI-authored.

question: How should the derived step start time be scoped -- does each row also carry an end time, does the display handle sessions that cross midnight, and does a row that has not started show its seeded registration timestamp?
decision: Start time only, no date handling, and no time at all on a row that has not started. A finished step's end is the next row's start one line below it; a session crossing midnight is left to the reader (the next row's hour being smaller says the day rolled over); a seeded plan row's dateTime is registration time and must never render as a start.

options.option: Start only, no date, nothing on an unstarted row (the operator's ruling).
options.consequence: One narrow grey field per started row. No duplicate data, no width spent on a case most sets never hit, and no risk of presenting a registration timestamp as a start -- which would be a fresh wrong signal of exactly the kind this set exists to remove.

options.option: Render start and end on every row.
options.consequence: Duplicate data on every row for no added information, since a finished step's end is already the next row's start.

options.option: Add date handling for sessions that cross midnight.
options.consequence: Costs width on every row to disambiguate a rare case, and the giveaway (a smaller hour on the next row) is already free.

options.option: Show the seeded row's own dateTime on an unstarted row.
options.consequence: Renders registration time as if it were a start -- a new wrong signal, worse than the silence this set is fixing.

operator_attestation: Operator rulings taken 2026-08-12 at spec authoring and recorded in docs/session-sets/127-the-active-step-shows-in-progress/spec.md under 'Operator rulings on the timestamp -- settled, do not reopen'; journalled verbatim at Session 1 registration.
rationale: These are display value trade-offs (information density versus row width versus the risk of a misleading signal) with no derivable right answer, so they are the operator's to make, and they were made at authoring. Journalled here as required by Session 1 Step 1 so the settled answers travel with the set and are not re-opened by a later session or a verifier. Session 2 renders these rulings; the UAT walk is where the operator sees the result of them, which is why this entry is tagged for the Decide section.
